sentence: This project builds a statistical and machine-learning framework and open-source software to help analyze data from sequencing newly transcribed RNA molecules.
This project provides advanced microscopy that lets researchers study the structure and behavior of cells and tissues related to diabetes.
This project studies how targeting two pathways in pancreatic cancer can limit tumor proliferation and induce an immune response.
This project uses sequencing to look for known and unknown organisms that cause infection in pigs and non-human primate xenograft recipients.
This project uses x-ray diffraction to study how mutations in sarcomere proteins change the structure and function of beating myocardium in transgenic pig hearts.
This project studies how paternal use of cocaine and methamphetamine in rats affects the behavior of offspring and grand-offspring through epigenetic mechanisms.
This project makes monoclonal antibodies against Candida auris, a fungus, and studies how they protect and work with antifungal drugs.
This project manages and analyzes research data with statistical methods and artificial intelligence to gain insights into aging and dementia.
This project studies how the glucocorticoid receptor affects the responses of macrophages and neutrophils to pathogens in larval zebrafish.
This project studies how chronic stress changes the way different types of striatal neurons respond to aversive stimuli.
This project uses models to study how brain changes in Alzheimer's disease occur at the functional and molecular levels.
This project studies two opposing signaling mechanisms that regulate mitochondrial remodeling.
This project builds data-driven methods to describe how proteins interact and to predict how immune receptors recognize their targets.
This project provides advanced microscopy and small animal imaging tools to investigate cancer biology at the cellular, sub-cellular, and organismic levels.
This project looks for sites on an ion channel where drugs could act, and studies how known inhibitors and activators bind there.
This project studies how Alzheimer's disease and hearing loss change signal conduction in the auditory brainstem of mammals.
This project builds a non-invasive wearable electrode device that monitors uterine contractions throughout the menstrual cycle.
This project studies how immunotherapy given before surgery changes the immune response in patients with recurrent glioblastoma.
This project uses real-world assessment methods to study how mood, pain, stress and social support relate to physical activity in people with diabetes.
This project develops strategies to build error correction into engineered systems so therapies and biotechnology work with greater specificity.
